documents.unit: Digital Futures Institute (TC AI and Pedagogy Working Group)
documents.title: TC Guidance: Developing a Generative AI Policy for Your Course
tiers: Permitted in Some Cases: Refer to Individual Assignments
Permitted in Some Cases: For Specific Purposes
Permitted in Some Cases: Confer with Instructor Prior to Use
Generally Permitted with Attribution or Disclosure
documents.summary: Digital Futures Institute guidance for TC instructors on writing a course generative AI policy. It lists factors to weigh and offers five adaptable syllabus statements from full prohibition to general permission with disclosure; the college sets no single rule.
documents.stance_why: The page sets no stance of its own: it says "TC encourages instructors to consider how generative AI can be integrated" and offers "five examples of syllabi statements reflecting varied stances" to "use and adapt as you see fit", so the decision is delegated to instructors via tiers.

units.why: The opening says "TC encourages instructors to consider how generative AI can be integrated into courses", a recommendation to instructors to weigh integration, so actor instructor, before-course, should. P02 is nearest (welcomes AI) though it only asks instructors to consider integration.
units.anchor: TC encourages instructors to consider how generative AI can be integrated into courses
units.fit_note: Encourages instructors to consider integrating AI; it is not a default rule that students may use AI and does not itself permit or require student use.
units.resolution_why: Coder A wrote a normalized policy, coder B left policy null. The anchor 'TC encourages instructors to consider how generative AI can be integrated into courses' already states the rule, so policy is null. Both coded instructor, before-course, should, P02, encourage; the fit note stays because the sentence asks instructors only to consider integration.

units.why: "be explicit and transparent in communicating this policy to students (in your syllabus, in class, and whenever relevant to assignments)" tells instructors to state their AI policy in several places; this is P09, phase course-start, should.
units.anchor: be explicit and transparent in communicating this policy to students
units.policy: Instructors are encouraged to be explicit and transparent in communicating their generative AI policy to students in the syllabus, in class, and whenever relevant to assignments.
units.resolution_why: Coders agreed on codes but A normalized the policy and B left it null. The anchor lacks its subject (instructors), so the normalized statement is kept, worded as the source does ('TC encourages instructors to ... be explicit and transparent in communicating this policy to students (in your syllabus, in class, and whenever relevant to assignments)').

units.why: The factor "Alignment with learning goals" lists what instructors should take into account when devising a policy; P83 ties AI decisions to learning objectives. Instructor, before-course, should.
units.anchor: Alignment with learning goals
units.policy: In devising a generative AI policy, instructors should take alignment with learning goals into account.

units.why: "Equity and access for all students" is a factor instructors should weigh in the policy; P51 covers equity and access, though the line names no concrete provision.
units.anchor: Equity and access for all students
units.frag_start: Equity and access for all students
units.frag_end: Equity and access for all students
units.policy: In devising a generative AI policy, instructors should take equity and access for all students into account.
units.fit_note: Names equity and access as a factor only; no concrete provision such as free access or alternatives.

units.why: "Information security and data privacy" is a factor to weigh; P50 is nearest but this is an instructor-side consideration, not a rule to protect data.
units.anchor: Information security and data privacy
units.policy: In devising a generative AI policy, instructors should take information security and data privacy into account.
units.fit_note: A consideration for instructors; no instruction to protect data or use vetted tools.

units.why: "Copyright and academic integrity" is a factor to weigh; P52 is nearest, though the line also names integrity.
units.anchor: Copyright and academic integrity
units.policy: In devising a generative AI policy, instructors should take copyright and academic integrity into account.
units.fit_note: Pairs copyright with academic integrity as one factor to weigh; only the copyright half is the type, and integrity is also named.
units.resolution_why: Types agreed (P52). A noted that only the copyright half fits and B that academic integrity is also named; fit notes merged and topics keep both intellectual-property and integrity-sanctions.

units.why: "five examples of syllabi statements reflecting varied stances" with "Please use and adapt as you see fit" gives instructors a menu of statements from prohibit to permit; P05 (named categories of use) is closest, and the choice is left to instructors.
units.anchor: five examples of syllabi statements reflecting varied stances on using AI in courses
units.frag_end: use and adapt as you see fit.
units.fit_note: A menu of sample statements from no use to open use that instructors choose or adapt; no table of uses per assessment.
units.resolution_why: Codes agreed. A wrote a normalized policy and B null; the anchor ('five examples of syllabi statements reflecting varied stances on using AI in courses') with 'use and adapt as you see fit' states it, so null. P05 over P04 because the point is the set of named tiers.

units.why: Example 1 states "Students are prohibited from using generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools to complete coursework or assignments", a ban on AI for all course work: P01, student, during-work, must-not.
units.anchor: Students are prohibited from using generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools to complete coursework or assignments

units.why: "Violation of this policy will be considered academic dishonesty" classifies prohibited AI use as misconduct handled by integrity procedures: P36, when-misuse, informs.
units.anchor: Violation of this policy will be considered academic dishonesty

units.why: 'Each assignment will specify whether AI can be used and, if so, how it should be employed' is the instructor's commitment to state the AI rule per assignment, so P04, actor instructor, course-start, must, and neutral because it only delegates.
units.anchor: Each assignment will specify whether AI can be used
units.frag_start: Students may use generative AI tools
units.frag_end: speak with me directly about your needs.
units.fit_note: Concerns an AI accommodation for disability; it does not say AI must be optional or free.
units.resolution_why: A coded phase during-work, modality informs, unit_stance restrict; B coded course-start, must, neutral. The source ('Each assignment will specify whether AI can be used and, if so, how it should be employed') is a syllabus commitment by the instructor to state expectations, not a mere fact (so must, not informs), and it communicates expectations (course-start). By itself it delegates the rule and neither allows nor limits AI, so neutral; the restriction is carried by the next unit ('may use ... for certain assignments where indicated').

units.why: Example 2: "Each assignment will specify whether AI can be used and, if so, how it should be employed" leaves the rule to each assignment: P04, instructor, course-start, must.
units.anchor: Each assignment will specify whether AI can be used
units.frag_start: If you are a student registered
units.fit_note: About a disability accommodation to speak to the instructor about; it does not say AI must be optional or free.

units.why: "Students may use generative AI tools for certain assignments where indicated" permits AI only where an assignment says so, so unindicated work is off limits. P04 fits as the sentence sets that assignments decide; P06 does not fit because it is about silence.
units.anchor: Students may use generative AI tools for certain assignments where indicated
units.frag_start: Students may use generative AI tools

units.why: "carefully read and follow these guidelines" makes students responsible for finding and following each assignment's AI rules: P78, student, during-work, must.
units.anchor: carefully read and follow these guidelines
units.policy: It is the student's responsibility to carefully read and follow each assignment's guidelines on AI use.
units.resolution_why: Coders agreed on codes; A gave a normalized policy because the anchor fragment has no subject or object. The source says 'It is the student's responsibility to carefully read and follow these guidelines' (the assignment's AI guidelines), so A's wording is kept.

units.why: "Students must include citations or disclosure detailing the specific AI tools and models used" requires disclosure naming tool and model; P25 over generic P24 because it names tool and model. Repeated in Examples 4 and 5; coded once.
units.anchor: Students must include citations or disclosure detailing the specific AI tools and models used
units.fit_note: Names tools and models only, not prompts or outputs.
units.resolution_why: Types, actor, phase and modality agreed. A coded unit_stance permit, B coded require. The source ('Students must include citations or disclosure detailing the specific AI tools and models used') is a condition on permitted AI use, not a requirement to use AI, so permit (require is for AI built into the work). A's fit note kept.

units.why: "Unauthorized use will be considered academic dishonesty" treats AI use beyond what the assignment allows as misconduct: P36, when-misuse, informs. Repeated in Example 4; coded once.
units.anchor: Unauthorized use will be considered academic dishonesty
units.resolution_why: Coders agreed on codes except unit_stance (A restrict, B neutral). 'Unauthorized use will be considered academic dishonesty' classifies misuse as misconduct (informs, a procedure), so neutral like the other misconduct statements in this document. The limit on use is coded in the neighbouring permission units.

units.why: Example 3 lists "helping you find background information about a topic" as a permitted use, using AI like a search tool for background: P12, may.
units.anchor: helping you find background information about a topic
units.frag_start: The use of generative AI tools
units.fit_note: Background research on a topic rather than understanding course concepts.

units.why: 'generating summaries or explanations of challenging material for your own reflection' is listed as a permitted study-aid use; P14 names summaries, so P14 over P12, which is about tutor-like help understanding concepts.
units.anchor: generating summaries or explanations of challenging material for your own reflection
units.policy: Generative AI tools may be used for generating summaries or explanations of challenging material for the student's own reflection.
units.fit_note: Also names explanations of challenging material, which is nearer P12 (understanding concepts); P14 chosen because summaries are named.
units.resolution_why: A coded P12 (explaining material for understanding), B coded P14 (study aids). The source lists 'generating summaries or explanations of challenging material for your own reflection'. Summaries are named in P14's definition, while P12 is about tutor-like help understanding concepts; the sentence bundles both, and P14 is chosen because summaries come first and 'for your own reflection' is study-aid use. The fit note records the explanation half; A's normalized policy is kept to show both parts.

units.why: 'drafting outlines to help you organize your thoughts' permits AI for outlining, which P91 covers (outlining, organizing writing); P15 is about idea generation and does not fit an outline of one's own thoughts.
units.anchor: drafting outlines to help you organize your thoughts
units.resolution_why: A coded P15 (with a fit note: only loosely brainstorming), B coded P91. P91's definition names outlining and organizing writing, so it fits directly; P15 is about idea generation and exploring alternatives, which outlining one's own thoughts is not.

units.why: "helping to improve grammar and style" permits AI editing support: P91.
units.anchor: helping to improve grammar and style

units.why: "Generative AI tools may NOT be used for any other purposes" bans every use outside the listed ones, a whitelist rule. No type states a catch-all limit to listed uses (P01 bans all use, P06 is about silence), so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: Generative AI tools may NOT be used for any other purposes
units.uncovered_note: AI is allowed only for the purposes the instructor lists and banned for every other purpose (a closed list of permitted uses). Coder A had put it under P05 with a fit note: the type is about named tiers, not a closed list.
units.resolution_why: A coded P05 with a fit note, B coded UNCOVERED. The source says 'Generative AI tools may NOT be used for any other purposes', a catch-all limit to listed uses. P05 is about named tiers or a table of uses; P01 bans all use; P04 delegates. The codebook prefers UNCOVERED over a stretched fit, so UNCOVERED with the note.

units.why: The template slot "specific prohibited uses, e.g. draft writing assignments, analyze data, etc" asks instructors to name banned uses, with examples; P19 is nearest.
units.anchor: specific prohibited uses, e.g. draft writing assignments, analyze data, etc
units.frag_start: you may not use AI to
units.policy: Students may not use AI for specific prohibited uses named by the instructor, for example to draft writing assignments or analyze data.
units.fit_note: A template placeholder for instructor-chosen banned uses (examples: drafting writing, analyzing data), not a fixed rule.
units.resolution_why: Both coded P19 must-not prohibit; A wrote a normalized policy, B left it null. The anchor is a placeholder ('specific prohibited uses, e.g. draft writing assignments, analyze data, etc') that does not itself state a rule, so A's normalized wording from 'you may not use AI to [...]' is kept. Fit notes merged.

units.why: "citations or disclosure detailing the specific AI tools and models used and how they were used" adds the manner of use to the disclosure; P25 is closest but it also asks how AI was used.
units.anchor: detailing the specific AI tools and models used and how they were used
units.frag_start: AI tools in this course are permitted
units.fit_note: Also requires describing how the tools were used, not only tool and model.

units.why: 'Students are allowed to use generative AI tools in their coursework only after obtaining explicit approval from the instructor' makes instructor approval the gate, so the rule is set by the instructor case by case: P04, student, must, restrict. P10 (ask when unsure) does not fit because approval is mandatory.
units.anchor: only after obtaining explicit approval from the instructor
units.frag_start: Students are allowed to use generative AI tools
units.fit_note: Approval by the instructor is a mandatory precondition for all AI use, decided case by case; the type is mainly about delegating the rule.
units.resolution_why: A coded P04 and phase before-course, B coded P10 and during-work. The source makes AI use depend on 'explicit approval from the instructor', so the decision rests with the instructor per use, which is P04; P10 is advice for unsure students, but here approval is required for all use. Approval is sought while students work on coursework, so during-work (before-course is for policy design).

units.why: "submit, in writing, a brief proposal outlining how the generative AI tool will be used" is a required written proposal before use. No type covers a pre-use proposal, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: submit, in writing, a brief proposal outlining how the generative AI tool will be used
units.frag_start: Prior to using any generative AI technology
units.frag_end: in the context of the assignment.
units.uncovered_note: Before using AI, students must submit a written proposal describing the intended use and purpose for the instructor to approve.
units.resolution_why: A coded P10 with a fit note and phase before-course; B coded UNCOVERED, during-work. The source requires a written proposal ('submit, in writing, a brief proposal outlining how the generative AI tool will be used') before any use. P10 is about asking when unsure, and a mandatory written proposal is a different procedure; UNCOVERED is preferred over a stretched fit. The proposal belongs to working on an assignment, so during-work.

units.why: "Approval will be granted based on the appropriateness and educational value of the proposed use" sets the criterion for approval, tying AI decisions to educational value; P83 is nearest.
units.anchor: Approval will be granted based on the appropriateness and educational value of the proposed use
units.fit_note: States approval criteria (appropriateness and educational value) and applies educational value to individual approval decisions rather than to course objectives.

units.why: Example 5: "generally permitted in this course for research and completion of assignments" allows AI by default: P02, student, may, permit.
units.anchor: Generative AI tools are generally permitted in this course for research and completion of assignments
units.frag_start: Generative AI tools are generally permitted
units.resolution_why: Codes agreed (P02, student, during-work, may, permit). A wrote a normalized policy that adds the attribution proviso; that proviso is a separate unit (P24), so policy is null and the anchor states the permission.

units.why: "all AI-generated content is clearly attributed as such" requires marking AI content as AI-generated in the submission: P24.
units.anchor: all AI-generated content is clearly attributed as such
units.frag_start: Generative AI tools are generally permitted
units.resolution_why: A coded unit_stance permit, B coded require. 'all AI-generated content is clearly attributed as such' is a condition attached to permitted AI use, not a requirement to use AI, so permit.

units.why: "Failure to properly attribute AI-assisted work will be considered academic dishonesty" makes nondisclosure the violation: P28 over P36 because the violation is the missing attribution.
units.anchor: Failure to properly attribute AI-assisted work will be considered academic dishonesty
units.resolution_why: Types agreed (P28, informs, when-misuse). A coded unit_stance permit, B neutral. 'Failure to properly attribute AI-assisted work will be considered academic dishonesty' states a sanction, a procedure, so neutral, consistent with the other misconduct units. P28 over P36 because the violation is the missing attribution.

notes: Single document: Digital Futures Institute guidance with five template syllabus statements (tiers). Units inside Examples 1-5 are coded as the policy each template statement would impose if an instructor adopted it. Sentences repeated verbatim across examples (accommodation, citation/disclosure, unauthorized use) are coded once per the exact-repeat rule; coder A's three extra repeats (Examples 4 and 5 citation, Example 4 unauthorized use) were dropped. No school or computing layer found; course layer deferred.
